section_title: What do poverty and wealth really say about a person?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 9 The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position. 10 But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field. 11 For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

context_lines: James now puts lowly circumstances and riches beside each other. The poor believer has a high standing to celebrate, while the rich person must face the lowliness that wealth can hide. Money cannot stop a human life from fading.

The flower makes the point concrete: its beauty does not keep the heat from withering it. James applies that passing beauty to the rich person in the midst of ordinary pursuits. The image recalls [Isaiah 40:6–8](https://biblehub.com/bsb/isaiah/40.htm), where human frailty stands beside God’s enduring word.
common_interpretation_lines: The shared emphasis is that poverty does not erase a believer’s dignity, and wealth provides no lasting reason for pride. [Calvin](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/james/1.htm) and [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-general-epistle-of-st-james/) both connect the poor believer’s high position with belonging to God and receiving His promised inheritance.
god_plan_lines: Jesus’ message to Smyrna in [Revelation 2:8–11](https://biblehub.com/bsb/revelation/2.htm) makes a similar contrast: He knows the church’s poverty yet calls it rich. The risen Christ sees a value that its outward circumstances cannot measure. That parallel helps explain why James can speak of a high position while the believer remains poor.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
